title: Explosive Semiconductor Growth in 2026 - Semiwiki
gist: The global semiconductor market hit a record $368B in Q2 2026 (+35% QoQ, +104% YoY) on AI-driven memory demand, with 2026 full-year forecasts now pointing to 90-112% growth (memory alone up 249-280%), while non-memory/non-AI suppliers grew a far more modest 9% QoQ—setting up a sharp deceleration into 2027 that analyst Bill Jewell still expects to be historically strong at ~50% growth.

themes.theme: Record-breaking 2026 growth, concentrated in memory and AI

insights.claim: The global semiconductor market reached $368 billion in Q2 2026 per WSTS, up 35% from Q1 2026 and up 104% year-over-year, both all-time records for sequential and annual growth.
insights.speaker: Bill Jewell
insights.so_what: Confirms the semiconductor cycle is not just recovering but experiencing unprecedented acceleration; investors should treat WSTS quarterly prints as a live gauge of AI capex translating into chip revenue.
insights.quote: The global semiconductor market in the second quarter of 2026 was $368 billion, according to WSTS. 2Q 2026 set records for growth: up 35% from 1Q 2026 and up a phenomenal 104% from 2Q 2025.

insights.claim: The prior growth record was set just one quarter earlier in Q1 2026, at +25% QoQ and +79% YoY, meaning the market has now broken its own growth record twice in a row.
insights.speaker: Bill Jewell
insights.so_what: Two consecutive record-breaking quarters indicates the growth is accelerating rather than plateauing, which raises the bar for what would constitute a slowdown signal in Q3/Q4 2026.
insights.quote: The previous record growth was set in 1Q 2026: up 25% from the prior quarter and up 79% from a year earlier.

insights.claim: Memory companies reported extreme sequential growth in Q2 2026 driven by AI demand: SK Hynix and Sandisk grew 51%, and Kioxia grew 76%, quarter over quarter.
insights.speaker: Bill Jewell
insights.so_what: Pinpoints memory (HBM/NAND/DRAM) as the epicenter of the current AI semiconductor boom—an investor should weight memory suppliers' guidance more heavily than logic/compute suppliers for near-term cycle signals.
insights.quote: Memory companies all reported extreme growth in 2Q 2026 from 1Q 2026 driven by AI applications, ranging from 51% at SK Hynix and Sandisk to 76% at Kioxia.
insights.locator: growth continues to be driven by AI paragraph

insights.claim: Kioxia and Sandisk have risen into the global top-10 semiconductor suppliers (ranked eighth and ninth) after each more than quadrupling revenue year-over-year on strong AI-driven flash memory demand.
insights.speaker: Bill Jewell
insights.so_what: A market-share reshuffling event: flash memory makers are vaulting up industry rankings, suggesting AI demand is broadening beyond DRAM/HBM into NAND flash and rewarding previously mid-tier suppliers.
insights.quote: They have benefited from the strong AI demand for flash memory. Each company has more than quadrupled revenue from a year ago.

insights.claim: Nvidia, the dominant AI processor supplier, grew a comparatively modest 18% quarter-over-quarter in Q2 2026, while Broadcom guided to 33% QoQ growth for the same quarter.
insights.speaker: Bill Jewell
insights.so_what: Nvidia's growth rate is now well below memory makers' triple-digit gains, suggesting the marginal AI capex dollar may be rotating toward memory/HBM supply constraints as much as toward GPU compute—watch memory pricing and allocation as a leading indicator alongside GPU shipments.
insights.quote: Nvidia, the dominant supplier of AI processors, grew 18% in 2Q 2026 from 1Q 2026. Broadcom, another significant AI supplier, projected 33% growth in 2Q 2026 in its 1Q 2026 guidance.
insights.locator: growth continues to be driven by AI paragraph

themes.theme: The growth is narrow, not broad-based

insights.claim: Excluding the major AI suppliers, the combined revenues of the rest of the top-20 semiconductor companies grew only 9% quarter-over-quarter in Q2 2026, far below the headline 35% market growth.
insights.speaker: Bill Jewell
insights.so_what: Critical for separating AI-exposed names from the broader chip market: an investor buying 'semiconductors' broadly is not getting AI-boom-like exposure unless concentrated in memory/AI-processor names specifically.
insights.quote: Excluding the major AI suppliers above, the combined revenues of the other top 20 semiconductor suppliers showed much more modest growth of 9% from 1Q 2026 to 2Q 2026.

insights.claim: Among non-AI-driven top suppliers, Q2 2026 revenue changes ranged from a 6% decline in Qualcomm's IC business to a 19% increase at Intel.
insights.speaker: Bill Jewell
insights.so_what: Shows meaningful dispersion even within the 'non-AI-boom' cohort—Qualcomm's IC weakness versus Intel's rebound suggests differentiated end-market exposure (mobile/handset weakness vs. Intel's PC/server/foundry recovery) worth separate analysis.
insights.quote: These companies' revenues ranged from a 6% decline in Qualcomm's IC business to a 19% increase at Intel.

insights.claim: The combined Q3 2026 guidance from non-AI-major suppliers points to just 6% sequential growth, indicating the broader chip market is normalizing even as AI/memory names remain hot.
insights.speaker: Bill Jewell
insights.so_what: A single-digit sequential guide from the broad market cohort confirms the boom is still narrowly concentrated in AI/memory, useful for stock selection versus sector-wide beta bets.
insights.quote: The combined guidance from these companies for 3Q 2026 is 6% growth from 2Q 2026.

insights.claim: Of twelve non-memory companies providing Q3 2026 guidance, only three (Qualcomm, Infineon, MediaTek) expect stronger growth than Q2, two (AMD, Onsemi) expect flat growth, and seven expect deceleration.
insights.speaker: Bill Jewell
insights.so_what: A majority-decelerating breadth reading among non-memory chipmakers is a caution signal for the broader semiconductor cycle even as headline AI/memory numbers stay spectacular—useful for rotation/timing decisions.
insights.quote: Of the twelve non-memory companies providing guidance, three (Qualcomm, Infineon Technologies and MediaTek) expect stronger growth in 3Q 2026, two (AMD and Onsemi) expect growth to remain the same, and seven project lower growth rates.

themes.theme: Deceleration ahead, but from an extreme base

insights.claim: The three memory companies giving Q3 2026 guidance (Micron, Kioxia, Sandisk) are projecting growth at less than half the pace of Q2 2026, signaling the memory boom's sequential growth rate is already decelerating even while remaining strongly positive.
insights.speaker: Bill Jewell
insights.so_what: Investors in memory names should model a deceleration in QoQ growth rates starting Q3 2026, even as absolute revenue levels stay elevated—key for setting realistic forward expectations versus extrapolating Q2's pace.
insights.quote: The three memory companies providing guidance (Micron, Kioxia and Sandisk) are projecting 3Q 2026 growth at less than half the rates of 2Q 2026.

insights.claim: Five recent full-year 2026 semiconductor market forecasts all project growth of 90% or more, with the highest at 112% from RCD Advisors and 101% from Semiconductor Intelligence itself.
insights.speaker: Bill Jewell
insights.so_what: A rare consensus among independent forecasters that 2026 will be roughly a doubling year for the chip market—an extraordinary base-rate departure investors should weight against historical mean-reversion risk.
insights.quote: Of the five latest forecasts, all call for an increase of 90% or more. The highest growth projections are 101% from us at Semiconductor Intelligence and 112% from RCD Advisors.

insights.claim: Memory is projected to be the primary driver of 2026 full-year growth, with WSTS forecasting 249% memory market growth and Gartner forecasting 280%.
insights.speaker: Bill Jewell
insights.so_what: Nearly triple- to quadruple-digit memory market growth forecasts represent one of the largest single-year sector moves in semiconductor history—memory capacity, pricing power, and capex plans (Samsung, SK Hynix, Micron, Kioxia) become the dominant swing factor for 2026 sector returns.
insights.quote: Memory will continue to be the major growth driver, with 2026 growth projections of 249% from WSTS and 280% from Gartner.

insights.claim: Most 2027 semiconductor market forecasts call for growth in the mid-twenty-percent range, with Semiconductor Intelligence projecting 50% growth for 2027 specifically.
insights.speaker: Bill Jewell
insights.so_what: Bill Jewell's 50% 2027 forecast is notably above the mid-20s consensus, an above-consensus bullish outlier worth tracking against actual 2027 prints as a test of his framework's accuracy.
insights.quote: We at Semiconductor Intelligence are projecting 2027 semiconductor market growth of 50%.

insights.claim: Semiconductor Intelligence's 2027 outlook assumes continued but less robust AI growth, healthy automotive and industrial markets, and a recovery in PC and smartphone markets as memory shortages ease.
insights.speaker: Bill Jewell
insights.so_what: Implies current memory shortages are actively suppressing PC/smartphone demand—an easing of memory constraints in 2027 would be a bullish catalyst for PC OEMs and handset makers, not just for memory suppliers themselves.
insights.quote: Recovery in the PC and smartphone markets as memory shortages ease

insights.claim: The current AI-driven semiconductor boom is characterized as eclipsing prior demand-driver eras: consumer electronics in the 1970s, PCs in the 1980s, internet infrastructure in the 1990s, and smartphones in the 2010s.
insights.speaker: Bill Jewell
insights.so_what: Frames the AI cycle as the largest structural demand shift in semiconductor history, useful context for sizing the scale of capex, capacity investment, and eventual overcapacity risk relative to past cycles.
insights.quote: The current AI driven boom eclipses previous periods driven by consumer electronics in the 1970s, PCs in the 1980s, internet infrastructure in the 1990s, and smartphones in the 2010s.

insights.claim: The author explicitly expects the current AI-driven semiconductor boom to eventually burst before settling into more sustainable growth, though the timing is uncertain.
insights.speaker: Bill Jewell
insights.so_what: A veteran semiconductor forecaster's explicit boom-bust framing (not just linear extrapolation) is a risk-management signal: even the most bullish near-term forecasts in this piece carry an implicit warning about eventual correction, relevant to positioning and hedging in memory/AI-chip equities.
insights.quote: The timing is difficult to predict, but the current AI boom will eventually burst and then settle into more sustainable growth.
